label: First order logic
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B10) states: A logic is first order if it has exactly one type.

label: Propositional logic
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05) states: A propositional logic is a logic in which the only objects are propositions , that is, objects which themselves have truth values.

label: Set theory
summary: PlanetMath (topic entry, MSC 03E30) states: Set theory is special among mathematical theories, in two ways: It plays a central role in putting mathematics on a reliable axiomatic foundation , and it provides the basic language and apparatus in which most of mathematics is expressed.

label: Model theory
summary: PlanetMath (topic entry, MSC 03C99) states: Model theory is a branch of mathematical logic which deals with the general problem of classifying mathematical structures.

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E10) states: An ordinal number is a well ordered set S such that, for every x ∈ S , x = { z ∈ S ∣ z < x } (where < is the ordering relation on S ).

label: Cardinal number
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E10) states: A cardinal number is an ordinal number S with the property that S ≤ X for every ordinal number X which has the same cardinality as S .

label: Recursive function
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03D20) states: Intuitively, a recursive function is a positive integer valued function of one or more positive integer arguments which may be computed by a definite algorithm .

label: Gödel’s incompleteness theorems

label: Lambda calculus
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B40) states: Lambda calculus (often referred to as λ -calculus) was invented in the 1930s by Alonzo Church, as a form of mathematical logic dealing primarly with functions and the application of functions to their arguments .

label: Logical connective

label: Logical language
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B15, 03B10) states: In its most general form, a logical language is a set of rules for constructing formulas for some logic, which can then be assigned truth values based on the rules of that logic.

label: Quantifier
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B15, 03B10) states: Introduction A quantifier is a logical symbol which makes an assertion about the set of values which make one or more formulas true.

label: Arithmetical hierarchy
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B10) states: The arithmetical hierarchy is a hierarchy of either (depending on the context ) formulas or relations .

label: Biconditional

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05) states: A truth function is a function that returns one of two values, one of which is interpreted as “true,” and the other which is interpreted as “false”.

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05) states: In classical propositional logic , an interpretation of a well-formed formula (wff) p is an assignment of truth (=1) or falsity (=0) to p .

label: Axiom of foundation
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03C99) states: The axiom of foundation (also called the axiom of regularity ) is an axiom of ZF set theory prohibiting circular sets and sets with infinite levels of containment.

label: Extension of a function
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E20) states: Let f : X → Y be a function and A and B be sets such that X ⊆ A and Y ⊆ B .

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 91F20, 68Q42, 68Q45, 03D05) states: Introduction A grammar , loosely speaking, is a set of rules that can be applied to words to generate sentences in a language .

label: Axiom of infinity
summary: PlanetMath (axiom entry, MSC 03E30) states: There exists an infinite set . The Axiom of Infinity is an axiom of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory .

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03-00, 65H05, 65H10) states: An empty set is a set ∅ that contains no elements .

label: Hilbert system
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03F03, 03B99, 03B22) states: A Hilbert system is a style (formulation) of deductive system that emphasizes the role played by the axioms in the system.

label: Injective function
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E20, 03E99) states: We say that a function f : A → B is injective or one-to-one if f ⁢ ( x ) = f ⁢ ( y ) implies x = y , or equivalently, whenever x ≠ y , then f ⁢ ( x ) ≠ f ⁢ ( y ) .

label: Surjective
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03-00) states: A function f : X → Y is called surjective or onto if, for every y ∈ Y , there is an x ∈ X such that f ⁢ ( x ) = y .

label: Uncountable
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E10) states: Definition A set is uncountable if it is not countable .

label: Ordering relation
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03-00, 81-00, 18-00, 17B37, 18D10, 18D35, 16W30) states: Let S be a set. An ordering relation is a relation ≤ on S such that, for every a , b , c ∈ S : • Either a ≤ b , or b ≤ a , • If a ≤ b and b ≤ c , then a ≤ c , • If a ≤ b and b ≤ a , then a = b .

summary: PlanetMath (topic entry, MSC 03E10) states: Ordinal arithmetic is the extension of normal arithmetic to the transfinite ordinal numbers.

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E10) states: Cardinality Cardinality is a notion of the size of a set which does not rely on numbers.

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03D05, 68Q45) states: An automaton is a semiautomaton with two types of special states: starting states, and final states.

label: Contradictory statement
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05) states: A contradictory statement is a statement (or form) which is false due to its logical form rather than because of the meaning of the terms employed.

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05, 03F07) states: The statement “ p is necessary for q ” “ q implies ( http://planetmath.org/ Implication ) p ”.

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B15) states: After the discovery of the paradoxes of set theory (notably Russell’s paradox ), it become apparent that naive set theory must be replaced by something in which the paradoxes can’t arise.

label: Axiom system for first order logic
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B10) states: Let FO ( Σ ) be a first order language over signature Σ .

label: Axiom system for propositional logic
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05) states: The language of (classical) propositional logic PL c consists of a set of propositional letters or variables , the symbol ⟂ (for falsity), together with two symbols for logical connectives ¬ and → .

label: Deduction
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03F03, 03B99, 03B22) states: Deductions are formalizations of proofs. Informally, they can be viewed as arriving at a conclusion from a set of assumptions, via applications of some prescribed rules in a finite number of steps.

label: Formal system
summary: PlanetMath (topic entry, MSC 03B99) states: In mathematical logic, a formal system is a “set-up” to study the syntactic structures of statements that we see in everyday mathematics.

label: Inference rule
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B35, 03B22, 03B05) states: In logic, an inference rule is a rule whereby one may correctly draw a conclusion from one or more premises .

label: Logical axiom
summary: PlanetMath (topic entry, MSC 03B22, 03B05) states: In a logical system , a logical axiom (sometimes called an axiom for short) is a logically valid (well-formed) formula used in a deductive system (particularly an axiom system ) to deduce other logically valid formulas.

label: Logically equivalent
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05) states: Two formulas A and B are said to be logically equivalent (typically shortened to equivalent ) when A is true if and only if B is true (that is, A implies B and B implies A ): ⊧ A ↔ B .

label: Modus ponens
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B22, 03B05, 03B35) states: Modus ponens is a rule of inference that is commonly found in many logics where the binary logical connective → (sometimes written ⇒ or ⊃ ) called logical implication are defined.

label: Normal modal logic
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B45) states: The study of modal logic is based on the concept of a logic , which is a set Λ of wff’s satisfying the following: • contains all tautologies , and • is closed under modus ponens .

label: Power set
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E99, 03E10, 37-01) states: Definition If X is a set, then the power set of X , denoted by 𝒫 ⁢ ( X ) , is the set whose elements are the subsets of X .

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03G99) states: A Chu space over a set Σ is a triple ( 𝒜 , r , 𝒳 ) with r : 𝒜 × 𝒳 → Σ .

label: Elementary recursive function
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03D20) states: Informally, elementary recursive functions are functions that can be obtained from functions encountered in elementary schools: addition , multiplication , subtraction , and division , using basic operations such as substitutions and finite summation and product .

label: Logicism
summary: PlanetMath (topic entry, MSC 03A05, 03-01) states: In the literature on the foundations of mathematics logicism aims at proving that the propositions of pure mathematics can be derived from the propositions of logic.

label: Multivalued function
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E20) states: Let us recall that a function f from a set A to a set B is an assignment that takes each element of A to a unique element of B .

label: Natural deduction
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03F03) states: Natural deduction refers to related proof systems for several different kinds of logic, intended to be similar to the way people actually reason.

summary: PlanetMath (theorem entry, MSC 03E25, 00-02) states: The principle of finite induction , also known as mathematical induction , is commonly formulated in two ways.

label: Reduced automaton
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03D10, 68Q42, 68Q05) states: Besides eliminating useless states that do not contribute to word acceptance, what else can we do to “clean up” an automaton ? In other words, we would like to reduce the number of states in an automaton to as small as possible without affecting its power of accepting words.

label: Reductio ad absurdum
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03-01) states: Reductio ad Absurdum is a process of inference by means of which one can derive a proposition ¬ ⁢ X from the fact the the assumption of X leads to a contradiction .

label: Semi-Thue system
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 68Q42, 03D40, 20M35, 03D03) states: A semi-Thue system 𝔖 is a pair ( Σ , P ) where Σ is an alphabet and P is a non-empty finite binary relation on Σ * , the Kleene star of Σ .

label: Sequent
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03F03) states: A sequent represents a formal step in a proof. Typically it consists of two lists of formulas , one representing the premises and one the conclusions .

label: Set difference
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03E20) states: Definition Let A and B be sets. The set difference (or simply difference ) between A and B (in that order) is the set of all elements of A that are not in B .

label: Sign relation
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 94A15, 94A05, 03G15, 03E20, 03B42, 03B10) states: A sign relation is a special type of triadic relation that arises in the use of signs to connote meanings and denote objects.

label: The inclusion of classical into intuitionistic logic
summary: PlanetMath (topic entry, MSC 03B20, 03A05, 03-01) states: Abstract The entry is a report of Gödel’s 1933 first proof of the consistency of classical arithmetic by means of an interpretation of the basic concepts of intuitionistic logic .

label: Church integer
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B40, 68N18) states: A Church integer is a representation of integers as functions , invented by Alonzo Church.

label: Comprehension axiom
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03F35) states: The axiom of comprehension (CA) states that every formula defines a set.

label: Paradox
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03A05, 03B99) states: A paradox is an assertion that is apparently self-contradictory, though based on a valid deduction from acceptable premises .

label: Polish notation
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 68N17, 03B70) states: Whereas operators are traditionally placed between operands, with parentheses used to override operator precedence , it is possible to place each operator to the left of its operands, thus eliminating ambiguity and the need for parentheses, and even the need for rules of operator precedence.

label: Reverse Polish notation
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 68N17, 03B70) states: Whereas operators are traditionally placed between operands, with parentheses used to override operator precedence , it is possible to place operators to the right of operands, thus eliminating ambiguity and the need for parentheses, and even the need for rules of operator precedence.

label: Cartesian product
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03-00, 81P10, 81P05) states: For any sets A and B , the Cartesian product A × B is the set consisting of all ordered pairs ( a , b ) where a ∈ A and b ∈ B .

label: Indexing set

label: Index set

label: Ordered tuplet
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03-00) states: The concept of ordered n -tuplet is the generalization of ordered pair to n items.

label: Universal relation
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B10) states: If Φ is a class of n -ary relations with x → as the only free variables , an n + 1 -ary formula ψ is universal for Φ if for any ϕ ∈ Φ there is some e such that ψ ⁢ ( e , x → ) ↔ ϕ ⁢ ( x → ) .

label: Functional completeness
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B05) states: Recall that in classical propositional logic , well-formed formulas (wffs) can be built up (recursively) from propositional variables via logical connectives .

label: Generalized quantifier
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03C80, 03B15, 03B10) states: Generalized quantifiers are an abstract way of defining quantifiers .

label: Second order logic
summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 03B15) states: Second order logic refers to logics with two (or three) types where one type consists of the objects of interest and the second is either sets of those objects or functions on those objects (or both, in the three type case).

label: Game-theoretical quantifier

summary: PlanetMath (definition entry, MSC 46A99) states: Definition A topological vector space is a pair ( V , 𝒯 ) , where V is a vector space over a topological field K , and 𝒯 is a topology on V such that under 𝒯 the scalar multiplication ( λ , v ) ↦ λ ⁢ v is a continuous function K × V → V and the vector addition ( v , w ) ↦ v + w is a continuous function V × V → V , where K × V and V × V are given the respective product topologies .
